title: Billboard anim frame not reset to 0 on idle/move state switch
claim: DFU MobilePersonBillboard.SetIdle (:291-313) resets currentFrame = 0 and animTimer = 1 on every idle<->move transition, so each state starts at frame 0. The port's MobilePerson.update (mobilePerson.js:245-256) keeps one monotonically increasing this.frame and this._timer across state changes and takes frame % n, so a transition starts at an arbitrary phase of the new record's cycle.
consequence: A townsperson stopping to face the player (or resuming walking) starts the idle/walk cycle at a random frame instead of frame 0 - a small visible animation-phase divergence.

title: place() marks the spawn tile Occupied; DFU never flags a spawn tile
claim: MobilePerson.place (mobilePerson.js:127-141) calls nav.setOccupied(gx, gy) on the spawn cell. In DFU nothing flags the spawn tile: SpawnAvailableMobile only positions the transform (PopulationManager.cs:150-166), GetRandomSpawnPosition only tests weight > 0 (CityNavigation.cs:512-535), InitMotor resets nav positions without setting flags (:274-283), and Occupied is only ever set on TARGET tiles in SetTargetPosition (:438-439). GetNextNavPositionWeight treats Occupied as weight 0 (:528-529), which the port mirrors, so the extra flag changes the neighbour weights other walkers see.
consequence: Until a just-spawned (or spawn-idled) person picks its first target, other townsfolk read its tile as weight 0 and path around it where DFU walkers would enter it - a subtle crowd-flow divergence.

title: Unsheathe always plays clip 78; DFU plays the weapon's own equip sound
claim: weaponRig.toggleSheath() plays SOUND.DrawWeapon (78) for every real weapon (weaponRig.js:104; playerWeapon.js:77-82; soundClips.js:11 calls 78 the 'FPSWeapon.DrawWeaponSound default'). In DFU that default is dead: WeaponManager.SetWeapon (:780) overwrites DrawWeaponSound with weapon.GetEquipSound() whenever ApplyWeapon (:742-755) applies a weapon, and ToggleSheath -> PlayActivateSound plays that field (FPSWeapon.cs:295). GetEquipSound (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:839-867) is per-type: 377/378/379/380/413/414/415/416 - none exist in the port's SOUND enum. The pin at test/weaponrig.test.js:31-37 restates the port, not the C#.
consequence: Every unsheathe of any real weapon plays the wrong clip: a flat draw sound 78 instead of DFU's weapon-specific equip clank (longsword 378, bow 416, etc.).

title: Bow viewmodel hidden during post-shot cooldown; DFU keeps it visible
claim: weaponRig.shown() returns false while `m.isBow && m.now < m.cooldownUntil` (weaponRig.js:75, 'bow cooldown hide'), so draw() skips the bow for the whole cooldown. DFU's WeaponManager.Update does `if (Time.time < cooldownTime) return;` (:230-233) BEFORE any ShowWeapons call - the early return leaves ScreenWeapon.ShowWeapon at its prior value (true, set at :290), so the bow stays drawn through the cooldown. Nothing in DFU hides a weapon for bow cooldown.
consequence: After every bow shot the port's bow art blinks out for the cooldown ((10*(100-speed)+800)/980 s, ~1.3s at speed 50) and pops back; DFU shows a steady idle bow.

title: Weapon stays drawn during the equip-delay pause; DFU hides it
claim: During an equip countdown DFU calls ShowWeapons(false) and returns (WeaponManager.cs:276-281), hiding the screen weapon until the delay expires. The rig ports only the attack-block half: attackInput/clickAttack test entity.equipCountdown (weaponRig.js:96,100, CH3 comment citing :276-278) and frame() drains it at dt*980 (:116-118, matching :679), but shown() (weaponRig.js:71-77) never consults equipCountdown, so draw() keeps rendering the newly equipped weapon through the pause. equip.js:56 sets entity.equipCountdown on every equip, so the state is reachable.
consequence: After swapping to a heavy weapon (EquipDelayTimes up to 5000) the port shows the new weapon immediately while silently refusing attacks; DFU shows empty hands for the delay - the player's cue the swap is in progress.

title: Jump gate misses the WasClimbing bypass; climbing.js wasClimbing is computed and never read
claim: AcrobatMotor.HandleJumpInput:76 gates the jump with `if (!climbingMotor.WasClimbing && playerMotor.GroundedTime < 0.1f) return;` - a player who was climbing at the start of this frame's check may jump with zero grounded time. The port's gate (motor.js:649) is `this.grounded && input.jump && this.groundedTime >= GROUNDED_JUMP_GATE_S && !this.slowFalling` with no climbing bypass. The port DOES track the flag - climbing.js:119 writes `this.wasClimbing = this.isClimbing` every step - but grep of src/ shows no reader anywhere: a ported member with no caller.
consequence: Topping out or aborting a climb onto ground then pressing Jump: DFU jumps instantly, the port refuses the jump for the next 0.1 s of grounded time.
